title: refactor(charts): delete the scatter's inert ZAxis declaration
body:
Fixes #9681

Clause-②: no

The scatter branch of `packages/plugin-charts/src/AdvancedChartImpl.tsx` declared a symbol-area envelope — a `ZAxis` element carrying `type="number" range={[60, 400]}` and **no `dataKey`**. It was inert. This deletes it, repairs the prose that derived a number from it, and leaves behind a test that states the painted mark size as a **reading** rather than as a declaration.

## The fork on the card is not reopened here

The card left one open — delete the declaration, or give it a `dataKey`. The dispatching seat ruled **DELETE**, by the floor and not by preference: variable-area marks do not exist in this product today, so wiring a `dataKey` **adds a capability** and is the maintainer's to take. ⛔ Nothing here prepares for that arm, and nothing here forecloses it either — a promise the tree does not keep is removed, that is all.

## Re-derived, not inherited — the declaration really was inert

⭐ This is the entire basis for calling the delete behaviour-neutral, so it was measured at this head rather than carried over from the card.

**Mechanism** (recharts 3.10.1, `es6/state/selectors/axisSelectors.js` + `es6/cartesian/Scatter.js`). The declared `range` is bypassed **twice over**:

1. `selectZAxisWithScale` returns `undefined` unless both the axis settings **and** a configured scale resolve. With no `dataKey` there is no domain, so no scale, so the registered axis never leaves the selector.
2. `computeScatterPoints` then takes `defaultRangeZ = zAxis ? zAxis.range : implicitZAxis.range`. With `zAxis` undefined it reads recharts' own `implicitZAxis.range`, which is `[64, 64]` — ⛔ **not** the declared `[60, 400]`. A point with no z value is painted at that range's lower bound, as a circle of `sqrt(area / PI)`.

**The discriminating number.** If any part of the declaration had reached a mark — even only as `defaultRangeZ[0]` — the radius would be `sqrt(60 / PI)` = **4.370193722368317**. Measured with the declaration still present, every mark's radius is **4.51351666838205** = `sqrt(64 / PI)`. The declared envelope contributes nothing.

**Where that measurement comes from.** Rendered through the same mechanism objectui#7396's edge-clipping suite documents: `ResponsiveContainer` replaced by an explicit 510x350 box, after which recharts computes the plot rect and every symbol's geometry arithmetically, with no DOM measurement in the path. ⚠️ I did **not** drive a real browser this round — the card's own Chromium reading stands on its own, and this run corroborates it: the six `cx` values measured here (65, 257.6, 300.4, 407.4, 450.2, 493) and the y-max row at `cy` 17 agree digit-for-digit with the post-fix real-Chromium row already recorded in that suite's docblock.

## Behaviour-neutral, proven by ablation

One ablation, both legs run from the **committed** implementation, restore pinned to `HEAD` and verified by hash rather than by an exit code:

| leg | file on disk | `ZAxis` element | result |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| A — after | `1787741c` (this commit) | 0 | 6 marks, all r = 4.51351666838205 |
| mutate | `cf72af1b` (the base blob, byte-identical to `origin/main`) | 1 | hash checked on disk before the run |
| B — before | `cf72af1b` | 1 | 6 marks, all r = 4.51351666838205 |
| restore | back to `1787741c` | 0 | `git diff HEAD` empty for the file |

⭐ The result is stronger than equal radii: **the whole rendered SVG is byte-identical between the two legs** — same length, same string, every `cx`/`cy`/`r` equal. Removing the declaration moves no pixel of this chart.

⚠️ Worth stating plainly, because the usual ablation expectation is inverted here: the new pin stays **green** under the mutation. That is not a pin that fails to measure — the claim being proved is *behaviour-neutrality*, so "the mutation changes nothing" **is** the result. The pin is on the painted size, ⛔ not on the declaration's absence.

## What was repaired alongside the delete

The one thing this delete could break was prose, and it was checked before the delete rather than after. objectui#7396's edge margin is sized to `sqrt(400 / PI)` — the declared envelope's **upper** bound, deliberately — so the margin already survives the day mark area becomes live. Deleting the declaration orphaned the justification, not the number:

- `SCATTER_SYMBOL_MAX_AREA`'s docblock said the scatter branch *declares* that envelope. It now names it as a **headroom budget** — the envelope a variable-area scatter would have to stay inside — and points at the instrument that reads what is actually painted.
- The `SCATTER_AXIS_EDGE_PADDING` "Why this size" section no longer derives its reasoning from a `dataKey`-less `ZAxis`.
- Two comments in `AdvancedChartImpl.scatterEdgeClipping-7396.test.tsx` that leaned on "the declared symbol envelope" / "the ZAxis range".

⛔ The margin **value** is unchanged, on purpose. Lowering it to what is painted today would tie the fix to a third-party default and re-open objectui#7396 the day mark area becomes variable.

A repo-wide sweep found no other carrier deriving anything from this declaration: outside the four sites above, no file in the tree mentions `ZAxis`, `60, 400`, `sqrt(400`, or a variable/bubble scatter size. No published `CHANGELOG` paragraph is touched.

## What is left behind, and why a pin rather than only a comment

The card's value is the class, not the two-character delete. Triage put the lesson on it because **the triage seat was itself the victim** — objectui#7396's triage comment read this live-looking declaration, reasoned correctly from it, and produced a bubble-size prediction every clause of which was false:

> 一条声明不是一条读数 … 惰性的声明和生效的声明,在源码里长得一模一样。

A comment alone would have been ceremony: it is the same kind of artifact that misled the last reader — prose asserting a fact, re-derived by nothing. So the delete ships with **both**, and the comment's job is only to point at the instrument:

- `AdvancedChartImpl.scatterSymbolSize-9681.test.tsx` — three assertions, each chosen for what its red would mean. Marks are **one size** across a 5x value spread (the clause the triage comment got wrong, stated as an assertion); the size is **identical across two fixtures four orders of magnitude apart** (so it is a property of the renderer, not of the data); and it is recharts' implicit default area (so a version bump that moves that default says so, instead of the margin's justification going quietly wrong).
- A comment at the scatter branch recording that mark area is recharts' own default and not configurable here — naming the test, ⛔ not restating its answer.

⚠️ The honest limit: this pin would **not** catch someone re-adding an inert declaration, because an inert declaration by definition changes nothing it can see. It catches the opposite and more useful case — the day the size stops being a constant, whoever did it must come to this file, restate the size, and re-check `SCATTER_SYMBOL_MAX_AREA`.

## Gates

Exit codes captured to a file before being read. Run at `7e82932`.

**The eslint run is a declared narrowing, and here is what makes it a measurement rather than a skip.** ① The population is CI's `turbo run lint`, i.e. every package's own `eslint .` — read from the root and package `lint` scripts, not guessed. ② Three files linted, counted from `--format json` output, not from my list. ③ Invariance for everything untouched: `eslint.config.js` sets no `parserOptions.project`, no `projectService` and no `tsconfigRootDir`, so no rule in this tree is type-aware; and no rule in `eslint-rules/` reads another file from disk (no `readFileSync` / `readdirSync` / `globSync` in any of them). ⇒ this diff cannot move the verdict on a file it does not contain. ⚠️ `check-lint-coverage` is **not** a second opinion on that and is not read as one — it validates that every package *has* a lint script; it runs no linter.

⚠️ `NOT MEASURED` locally, left to CI: the repo-wide `pnpm test` shards, `pnpm test:dist`, `test:e2e`, `pnpm check` (the CLI self-check), and the remainder of the `check:*` farm whose inputs this diff does not touch.

## Acceptance notes

⛔ Nothing below is filed, and nothing below is repaired here.

- **The bounded census the card asked for (is anything else inert for the same reason?) came back empty, within a stated bound.** `packages/plugin-charts` contains exactly one `ZAxis` — the one deleted — and every recharts symbol imported by `AdvancedChartImpl.tsx` has a real JSX use site, so there is no dead import of the same family. The one other "declared but conditionally ignored" shape I went looking for, `minTickGap` beside an `interval={0}`, does not occur on the same element. ⚠️ The bound, stated so it is not read as more than it is: this enumerated declarations at their use sites: it did **not** prove every recharts prop in the file live, and no instrument in this repo does.
- **`check-changeset-claims` asked for one paragraph to be re-read: `.changeset/7546-chart-series-keys-declared.md`, which names `AdvancedChartImpl.tsx`.** Read. It claims six series keys (`label`, `variant`, `opacity`, `dashArray`, `stack`, `yAxis`) do real work in this file. This diff moves none of them — it deletes a z-axis prop and edits comments — and each of the six still has live references in both `AdvancedChartImpl.tsx` and `normalizeChartSchema.ts`. Nothing in that body goes false because of this change. **Carrier for anything further: none — this change does not touch it.**
- **That same pending changeset body carries a cross-file line address (`normalizeChartSchema.ts:242-255`), the form AGENTS.md #11 bans outright.** ⛔ Noted, **not filed**, and deliberately not repaired: the repo has already ruled this population — existing citations are repaired *opportunistically when you are in the file anyway* and ⛔ never swept, with `census:cross-file-line-citations` reporting the tree-wide picture by design. Filing a card for one instance would act against that standing ruling. ⚠️ The one thing worth recording, since nothing else does: a *pending changeset* is the carrier where "opportunistically" has a deadline, because the body publishes verbatim into a CHANGELOG and AGENTS.md then forbids re-addressing it. **Carrier: the next seat that edits that changeset, or the release that publishes it.**
- **If variable-area scatter marks are wanted, that is a feature card with its own appetite** — it needs a `dataKey` and the schema key to feed it. ⛔ Not this repair, and nothing here blocks it: the edge margin is already sized to the envelope such a feature would live inside.
